validation.notes: Production fix: DefaultResourceLoader.loadProjectTrustExtensions() in packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts forced project trust to true (setProjectTrusted(true)) despite the comment requiring an untrusted bootstrap, so project-local extensions were resolved and loaded before the user approved the project. It now forces false, then reloads settings, then resolves extensions. The regression uses the read-only subject.mjs boundary fakes against the real loader lifecycle: (1) starting from a previously trusted state, the bootstrap callback sees only user.ts + cli.ts (no project.ts), the event order is set(false) -> settings(false) -> resolve(false) -> extensions(user,cli), and after the resolver returns true the final set is cli.ts + project.ts + user.ts; (2) a declined resolver leaves trust false and never loads project.ts; (3) plain reload() without a trust bootstrap still honors the current trust state in both directions, so the fix is scoped to the bootstrap pass. Verified the script exits 0 on the repaired code and exits 1 with AssertionError 'bootstrap must expose user/global and CLI extensions but no project extension' (actual [cli.ts, project.ts, user.ts]) when line 438 is temporarily reverted to setProjectTrusted(true). Limitation: the package test suite (vitest, e.g. packages/coding-agent/test/resource-loader.test.ts) could not be run because dependencies are not installed in this workspace and installing them is out of scope; the regression relies only on Node 24 built-ins (node:assert, node:path, node:vm via subject.mjs).
